pr.title: Save K in 16-token blocks, shared with idle worker threads
pr.head: dfafd13dce

short_version: PR #4898, the third of the four PRs that split PR 4424, stores the VNNI-packed K rows (the key vectors of attention) of up to 16 tokens as whole 64-byte lines after a register transpose, and lets the idle main helper threads of a generated plugin share that store with the main thread.

The page introduces the two data models (the K store window batch::k_store_window_t and the work unit), the three algorithms (the register transpose of store_block, the run cut k_store_cut_units and the per-run store store_k_block), the two policies (the sharing decision k_store_shared and the partial-block path) and the two protocols (the open / claim / join window of save_k_impl with its watchdog, and the save_k entry points with their generated call sites) that the PR adds, carried by K_VNNI-B3, KV_CACHE-B2 and MODEL-B1 to MODEL-B5.

For each diagram the page says which boxes land in this PR, which were there already (from main, PR #4868 or PR #4887), and which land only in PR #4901 (the saved-row bits, the row-major tail block and the forward-end conversion).

words.definition: The same configuration run twice (new against new2 in the PR body). It measures the run-to-run noise of a measurement.

C++ std::memory_order values. A release write publishes every earlier write of its thread to a thread whose acquire read sees the stored value, acq_rel does both, and relaxed orders nothing beyond the atomic itself.

Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. The AMX kernel qk_vnni_128x4 reads a page's VNNI-packed K plane as its B operand (the second matrix of the tile multiply), and this PR adds no AMX instruction.

The attention workers' per-page scoring routines of self_attention.hpp. apply_dense_amx_page runs the AMX kernel on a full page [1749, 1782], and apply_page_tok runs the software readers (qk_group for a VNNI slot [1856, 1994]) and calls apply_dense_amx_page at 1909.

The threads that run the attention kernels of a layer. Their pending sections (the attention work that waits for a page's latch) wait behind save_k, and they read a page only after every minibatch that writes it counted the latch down [model.hpp:3088].
The CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set, with 16 lanes of 32 bits per register. The loads, the transpose and the stores of store_block, and the reader qk_group, are AVX-512 code.

One of the 16 drawings of the three PR 4424 source pages (data, type, function, sequencing, interaction and decision models), copied unchanged with line numbers that cite PR 4424 head 9d5c7a389b, not this PR's head. This page says what of each lands in this PR.
The 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K values. One 128-dimension K row is 128 bf16 = 256 bytes.

16 consecutive page offsets of one page (offsets 16 c to 16 c + 15 for block c): one AMX tile width and the unit of the block save. k_store_block is model.hpp's name for the constant [model.hpp:3142].

The store of the K rows of up to 16 tokens of one block as whole 64-byte lines after a register transpose. page::set_k_block is the page entry point and store_block the operation [kv_cache.hpp:2042-2049; tensor/k_vnni.hpp:381-406], and its result is bit-identical to the per-row store per present token.
The struct that owns the KV memory of a request: its pages, its storage slots and the kv_blocks inside them.
64 bytes, the unit the CPU caches move. The window keeps the claim counter next_unit and the polled counter opened on separate lines [common.hpp:1174-1178].

Main's serial part of a layer, the time that no other thread shortens (the thick red frame of MODEL-B4). The Note calls the per-row store the main thread's largest serial piece of work in a prefill layer [model.hpp:3083-3084].
Twice the larger of the two binaries' sample standard deviations over 3 repetitions, never smaller than 0.4 TPS or 0.15 s. A difference beyond the band counts as a change.

Prefill processes the prompt (many tokens per user per pass), and decode generates one token per user per step (one item per user per pass). The PR body's decode cells run 8 users, 8 items per decode pass, below the sharing threshold of 16 items [model.hpp:3160-3162].
Dimensions 2 dp and 2 dp + 1 of one token share one 32-bit lane (a dword, 4 bytes). A 512-bit register has 16 such lanes, one per token of a block.
32 dimensions = 16 dimension pairs, 4 steps per 128-dimension head. store_block runs its transpose once per step.
The AVX software reader for row-major K: one dot product per (query head, token). PR #4901 uses it for the rows of a row-major tail block.

A speculation model whose KV storage has its own extra physical slot in the book. The names book::eagle_view_active and EAGLE_STORAGE_SLOTS_1 in the later-PR lists are PR #4901's, and this PR changes nothing of EAGLE.
The atomic add that returns the counter's old value. The claim on next_unit and the counts on opened and finished use it [model.hpp:3336, 3345, 3351].
One forward() call that runs every layer for this step's tokens. The forward end is the part of run_forward after the plugin's run() returned [model.hpp:1836-1853].
FPGA = field-programmable gate array, the accelerator card, and hardware attention is attention scored on it. The policy for blocks under hardware attention is PR #4901's.

A generated plugin is the model code that the code generator ingest/src/TronCpp.hs emits, with a main thread that runs run() and helpers that run run_main_help. Handwritten plugins (h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp:1038-1039) and the unit tests call save_k with the default worker arguments (0 and 1) and never share [model.hpp:3102-3104], except the three-thread section of the save_k case (t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3988-4108), which passes worker_ix and n_workers = 3.

A GOF is a group of 4 consecutive tokens whose K/V rows the staging (gof::populate) copies into a buffer for the FPGA. Idle attention workers run that work through help_drain_gof, and main drains the rest in wait_for_coop_gof at the forward end [model.hpp:3503, 3516].
The Intel Xeon 6962P server with AMX (delphi-3bda) on which the PR body's measurements were taken.

Working files of the page's verification. hits.txt counts, for each identifier of a diagram box, its occurrences in main's tree and in the added lines of each of the four PR diffs, and files-4901.txt lists the files PR #4901 touches.

The join is main's wait until every helper has incremented finished. The watchdog reads the clock once every k_join_clock_spins = 1,048,576 _mm_pause loops (_mm_pause is a CPU hint instruction that slows a polling loop and saves power) and aborts k_join_timeout_s = 120 s after the first clock read, with the finished-helper and claimed-unit counts in the message [model.hpp:3145-3151, 3354-3368].

K is the key matrix of attention, and a K row is one token's 128 bf16 values for one KV head in dimension order. ks is the K buffer of the minibatch that save_k reads (its tron record label is 'WK roped').
The check in apply_page_tok that every block of a page is VNNI-packed before the dense AMX path runs. It lands in PR #4901 (self_attention.hpp:1924-1935 at the PR #4901 head 175b1837b9).

The owner of one 16 KiB K plane, its matrix view, and the one friend route from a view to the raw plane address. store_block takes a writable view and reaches the plane through k_vnni_access::plane [tensor/k_vnni.hpp:189, 143, 218-222, 386].

words.term: kernel PR / layout PR / tail-block PR / this PR (the stack)
words.definition: The four PRs, each based on the previous one: PR #4868 (the layout PR: VNNI-packed K layout, the per-row store, the reader), PR #4887 (the kernel PR: the AMX kernel), PR #4898 (this PR: the shared block save) and PR #4901 (the tail-block PR: the row-major tail block, the page bits, the forward-end conversion, the hardware-attention policy, and the option on in the deb preset, the package-build preset).
TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 in the environment prevents use of the AMX kernels at run time. It leaves both store paths of this PR untouched.
One key/value head. Each token has n_kv_heads of them, and store_k_block stores every KV head of each token of a run.
A page holds 64 contiguous tokens of K and V per storage slot and KV head, and a page offset is a token's position inside its page (0 to 63). Block c of a page is offsets 16 c to 16 c + 15.
The struct that holds the K plane and the V plane of one (storage slot, KV head, page). kv_block::k is the typed owner k_vnni_tensor for a VNNI slot since the layout PR [kv_cache.hpp:2554-2564].
A countdown synchronisation object (latch_ref) with wait() and count_down(). batch::upstream_kvs_ready is the per-slot latch the downstream attention waits on.
One transformer layer of the model. save_k runs once per (layer, minibatch) pass.

k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, the compile-time gate: true for 128-dimension heads with the option on, false otherwise. k_store_shared and store_k_block branch on it [tensor/k_vnni.hpp:105-108; model.hpp:3157, 3214].

load_row is the inverse of store_row (4 gathers that read one token's row out of a plane [tensor/k_vnni.hpp:351]), and copy_token copies one token between planes through load_row and store_row [415]. page::k_packed is the read-only view of a plane that the two score kernels take [kv_cache.hpp:2005-2009].
The Haskell test suite of the code generator (ingest/test/LoopyTronSpec.hs). Two of its specs check the text of both generated save_k calls.

words.term: main thread / main helpers / worker_ix / n_workers / run_main_help
words.definition: The main thread runs the schedule of a generated plugin, and the main helpers run its per-token kernels through run_main_help. worker_ix is 0 for main and 1 to n_workers - 1 for the helpers, and n_workers = 1 + the number of main helpers [TronCpp.hs:1392, 1363-1365].

The per-token completion mark, the GOF credit and the downstream minibatches' latch that save_k counts down after every row is stored. All three are main code that runs after the join [model.hpp:3372-3388].
The loop of save_k_impl over q_batch->items after the join. It writes the per-token completion marks and the GOF credits [model.hpp:3372-3385].

words.term: minibatch / batch / items / token job / token_jobs_do_kv
words.definition: A minibatch (struct batch) is one chunk of the pass's token jobs that run together, listed in order in q_batch->items. token_jobs_do_kv says whether a job writes KV.

words.term: Note [Shared block save] / Note [K VNNI storage] (a Note)
words.definition: A Note is a named comment block in the tron source. Note [Shared block save] (model.hpp:3078-3139) is this PR's design record, and Note [K VNNI storage] (kv_cache.hpp:651) says who writes and reads the VNNI-packed layout.
The CMake option, default OFF, which when on selects VNNI-packed K storage for every 128-dimension head. It stays off in every preset until PR #4901.

words.term: page copies, clears and the staging callback (book::append, copy_from, copy_storage_slot, clear_kv_complete_at, fill_storage_slot, k_head_fn)
words.definition: book::append copies a page's slots between books through page::copy_from and copy_storage_slot [kv_cache.hpp:1254, 1282, 2350, 2308], clear_kv_complete_at clears a page offset's completion state when a new token takes the offset [2213], and book::fill_storage_slot fills a storage slot with values from a random distribution [1722-1723]. page_info::k_head_fn is the staging gather's callback that reads one K row through get_k_row [full.hpp:2747, 2759].
One 64-byte line of a panel: one dimension pair of 16 consecutive tokens, one dword per token.
One 1 KiB tile of a plane for one dimension step s and one token block c (16 pair rows of 64 bytes), which is one AMX B tile. store_block fills one panel per (step, block) with 16 line stores.
The store of one token's K row into the VNNI-packed plane with 4 AVX-512 scatters, 4 bytes into each of the token's 64 lines (the layout PR). At this PR's head a run of one token still takes it.
K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, stored as 16 panels.
PR 4424 (branch jhan-amx-vnniK, 4,054 lines) is the original PR that the four PRs replace. The three source pages diagram its three files at head 9d5c7a389b.

words.term: present mask / FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF / masked store / k_scatter_run_len
words.definition: The present mask is the 16-bit lane mask of the block's tokens that the run holds (FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF is the all-present value), a partial block uses line stores masked to the present lanes, and k_scatter_run_len = 1 is the run length that takes the per-row store instead [tensor/k_vnni.hpp:80-81, 396-406; model.hpp:3144, 3263]. PR #4901 removes the mask parameter from set_k_block and the constant k_scatter_run_len, and keeps FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF as the value set_k_block passes to store_block.
The prompt length in tokens of a measurement cell (runtron --prompt-length). Every run then generates 256 tokens.
k_vnni::qk_group, the AVX-512 routine of the layout PR that scores a query group (the query heads sharing one KV head) against one VNNI-packed page [kernels/k_vnni.hpp:62].
The AMX kernel of the kernel PR that reads the VNNI-packed plane as its B operand [amx_attn.cpp:237; amx_attn_iface.hpp:267].
The 4-billion-parameter model used in the PR body's measurements.

rope is the rotary position embedding applied to the Q and K rows before the store, and nothing blocks between a helper's rope kernel and its save_k call [model.hpp:3135-3136]. The K channel is the buffer whose readiness main waits for before save_k (startOperand in the generated run(), TronCpp.hs:2937; main renamed it startReadingAll in commit d3e4297df6, after the stack's base 72308ec90c).

Row-major is the layout with one contiguous 256-byte row per token. The row-major tail block of PR #4901 keeps a block row-major until its 16th row is saved, and at this PR's head no block is row-major in a VNNI slot.
Consecutive items of the minibatch that fall in the same 16-token block of the same page, with no page offset repeated. store_k_block collects one run at a time [model.hpp:3240-3262].

save_k (two overloads) is the entry point that stores the K rows of one minibatch, and save_k_impl runs the window protocol. k_store_shared decides the sharing, k_store_cut_units cuts the items into work units, and store_k_block stores the runs of one unit [model.hpp:3398-3416, 3304, 3156, 3168, 3204].

note_k_row_saved and note_k_block_saved publish the page bits k_rows_saved_ (one per page offset) and k_vnni_blocks_ (one per block), and convert_pending_k_blocks converts the blocks listed in pending_k_blocks_ at the forward end through k_block_to_vnni_at and block_to_vnni. None of these names, nor the row-major readers and clears block_to_rows, row_major_row, k_row_if_row_major and k_forget_row, exists at this PR's head.
An AVX-512 store that writes 16 dwords to 16 separate addresses. store_row issues 4 of them per token.
The last entry of the unit table, unit_start[n_units] = the item count. It marks the end of the last unit [model.hpp:3192].
A loop that re-reads a variable until it changes, instead of sleeping. The helper's wait for opened and main's join on finished are spins [model.hpp:3339-3341, 3356-3368].
split-plan-3.1.md, the plan that assigned the changes of PR 4424 to the four PRs. Its item U2.1 keeps the masked partial-block path in this PR and lets PR #4901 delete it.
One K/V storage unit of the book, selected by kv_slot_id. One attention operation writes one slot (binding.kv_slot).
Two C++ unit-test binaries. The block-save case is in t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:207-262. The save_k case with its one-thread and three-thread sections is in t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3800-4109.
Token t of a block owns lane t (column t % 16) of every pair row of its block. Two threads that write different tokens of one block write different lanes.
Tensor parallel over 2 or 4 devices.

One token's 128 values in dimension order, with the caller's alignment and DMA (direct memory access) flags as template parameters. k_source_row and k_destination_row build one from a bf16 pointer [tensor/k_vnni.hpp:243-260].
The in-place transpose of 16 registers of 16 dwords, in four stages of 16 two-register shuffles (64 shuffles). After it, register i holds pair row i of the panel [tensor/k_vnni.hpp:294-320].
tron is the inference program under test. runtron is its command-line tool.
TTFT = time to first token, the prefill latency. TPS = decode tokens per second.

VNNI = Vector Neural Network Instructions, and VNNI-packed means stored in the VNNI layout. That layout is the right-operand format of the AMX tile multiply: two consecutive dimensions of one token are adjacent in memory, and one 64-byte line holds that dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens.
A diagram form with one lane per thread, time left to right, solid blocks for work and dashed outlines for waiting (MODEL-B4).

The window is the per-minibatch record of one shared K store [common.hpp:1170-1193], with the unit table unit_start (unit u = items[unit_start[u], unit_start[u + 1])) and n_units, the claim counter next_unit, opened (windows opened in this pass), finished (helpers done with the open window), and helper_windows (the windows each helper has entered, by worker_ix). A work unit is a run of consecutive items in one 16-token block of one page with the same token_jobs_do_kv value.
The example the three source pages trace: token 37, dimension 70 of the plane of storage slot 5, KV head 0, page 7, and a 40-item window with 3 workers.

what_lands.concept: The block save: store_block, transpose_16x16_epi32 and page::set_k_block
what_lands.where: h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:80-83, 91, 95-96 (FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF, LANES_16 and their static_asserts), 294-320 (the transpose), 365-406 (store_block); h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2031-2049 (set_k_block), 666-667 and 678-690 (Note [K VNNI storage] item 1)
what_lands.note: For each of the 4 dimension steps, store_block loads one 64-byte piece per present row with AVX-512 loads. It transposes the 16 registers in place. Then it writes the panel's 16 pair rows as whole lines, masked to the present lanes when the block is partial. The same 4 KiB as 16 per-row stores is written, with 64 line stores instead of 64 scatters of 4 bytes into 16 lines each.

One record per minibatch: the unit table unit_start and n_units, the claim counter next_unit, the counters opened and finished, and helper_windows. next_unit and opened sit on their own cache lines. So a claim does not invalidate the line the waiting threads poll.

A unit is a run of consecutive items in one 16-token block of one page with the same token_jobs_do_kv value. Unit u is items[unit_start[u], unit_start[u + 1]). Two threads that store different units of one block write different token lanes.

Main walks the items once before it opens the window. It starts a unit at every change of the (kv, page, block) key. It writes the end sentinel (unit_start[n_units] = the item count, the end of the last unit) and n_units last.

Main and every helper decide from the same inputs: a VNNI slot (the option on and a 128-dimension head), 2 to 128 workers, and more than 16 items. So a helper never waits for a window that main does not open.

what_lands.concept: store_k_block: one run becomes one set_k_block or one set_k_row
what_lands.note: For a VNNI slot the function collects a run: consecutive KV items of one block of one page, where a repeated offset ends the run. It stores a one-token run with set_k_row, and a run of 2 to 16 tokens with set_k_block and the present mask. Row-major slots keep one page::k(...).set per token, moved here from the marks loop. A non-bf16 K buffer is converted to bf16 on the stack first.

what_lands.concept: The window protocol: open, claim, join, and the join watchdog (save_k_impl)
what_lands.note: Main cuts the units, zeroes next_unit and finished, and increments opened with release. A helper's W-th call waits with acquire until opened >= W. Every thread claims units with fetch_add (acq_rel) and stores them. A helper increments finished with release and returns. Main spins with acquire on finished until every helper is done, under a watchdog that aborts 120 s after its first clock read. Then main writes the completion marks and GOF credits and counts the downstream latches down.

what_lands.concept: The save_k entry points with worker_ix and n_workers, and the generated call sites on both sides
what_lands.where: h/tron/models/model.hpp:3391-3416; ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:2864-2882 (the helper-side call in runHelperStatement), 2936-2944 (the main-side call with the literal 0 in saveKv)
what_lands.note: Both save_k overloads take worker_ix = 0 and n_workers = 1 as defaults. The generated run() passes 0 and n_workers, and the generated run_main_help passes the helper's worker_ix and n_workers at the same statement position. So the N-th window a helper enters in a pass is the N-th window main opens.

what_lands.concept: The partial-block path: k_scatter_run_len, the present mask through set_k_block, and store_block's masked stores
what_lands.note: At this PR's head a run of 2 to 15 tokens is stored as one masked block store. PR #4901 replaces that path: a run shorter than 16 is stored row by row into the row-major tail block, and set_k_block loses its mask parameter (split plan U2.1). MODEL-B5 draws the PR #4901 form.

what_lands.concept: Tests: the block-save case, the three-thread save_k section, the LoopyTronSpec call-text checks
what_lands.where: t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:207-262; t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3800-4109 (one thread 3980-3986, three threads 3988-4108); ingest/test/LoopyTronSpec.hs:3122-3138, 3547-3553
what_lands.note: The block-save case compares store_block against store_row per present token bit for bit over 4 blocks and 38 masks. The three-thread section starts one helper 20 ms late, reads the finished count as the main call returns, and checks the unit invariant (each unit lies in one page, one block and one KV-write state). The two Haskell specs check both generated call texts.

walkthrough.say: This is the third PR of four. The layout PR stored each token's K row with 4 scatters that write 4 bytes into each of the token's 64 lines. That store was the main thread's largest serial piece of a prefill layer: 0.86 ms per layer in the 2026-09-14 trace [model.hpp:3081-3089]. This PR stores a run of tokens as whole lines after a register transpose, and lets the idle main helpers share the store. Time to first token falls by 153 ms at tp2 and by 243 ms at tp4 at prompt 1,024 tokens against the kernel PR, and decode TPS stays inside the decision band. The kill switch (TRON_AMX_DISABLE) leaves both store paths of this PR untouched [kv_cache.hpp:689-690].

Point at the plane, its 16 panels (s, c), and the pair rows of one panel: one 64-byte line holds one dimension pair for 16 tokens. All of this is the layout PR's. The constants are at tensor/k_vnni.hpp:58-79 and the index map at 113. Say that store_block writes one panel at a time, the four panels (s, c) of one block c. The two state words in the page column and the orange frame (a block that is still row-major) belong to PR #4901.

Point at 'block c = panels (s, c)': block c owns four 1 KiB panels, 4 KiB apart. The store_block box is this PR's [tensor/k_vnni.hpp:381-406], and its panel address is plane + (s * 4 + c) * 512 elements [395]. The store_row box is the layout PR's per-row store that the block save replaces for runs of 2 to 16 tokens. The row-major form, store_row_major, block_to_vnni, block_to_rows and the block bit are PR #4901.

Open the whole-block group: store_block [tensor/k_vnni.hpp:381-406] loads one 64-byte piece per present row (the 16 pairs of step s), calls transpose_16x16_epi32 [294-320], then writes the panel's 16 pair rows as whole lines [396-406]. Its callers are page::set_k_block [kv_cache.hpp:2042-2049] and store_k_block [model.hpp:3291]. The index and view groups and store_row, load_row and copy_token are the layout PR's. The row-major group, the conversion group, the bit helpers and the callers note_k_row_saved, k_forget_row, k_layout_dense and k_row_if_row_major are PR #4901.
